body:
- For example, in the user input, it can just ask "run two steps" and the orchestrator can stop there. 
- So taking this input, instead of running non-stoppingly for many steps, it will interpret user input and stop ahead. 
- but i am not sure in which way this will impact other routes?

@sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
Yes, I think this should be supported, but as an **orchestrator-only stop budget**, not as a new public route.

Current state:
- The planner already has a `stop` decision in [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md).
- Runtime already honors planner stop and max-round exhaustion in [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts).
- `/orchestrate` enters through [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml), then dispatches [`agent-orchestrator.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml).
- Follow-up routes only hand back when `orchestration_enabled == 'true'`, so direct `/implement`, `/review`, and `/fix-pr` should stay one-shot.

Recommended approach:
1. Parse explicit bounded-step language from the original `request_text`, for example “run two steps”, “stop after 2 actions”, “do one pass”.
2. Convert that into an effective orchestration budget before dispatching follow-up work.
3. Preserve the existing hard cap from `automation_max_rounds`.
4. Tell the planner about the user-requested limit so it can choose `stop` naturally when the requested number of steps is reached.
5. Add tests around the off-by-one behavior.

Important detail: current `automation_current_round` starts at `1` before the first dispatched action. So if the user says “run two steps”, we need to decide whether that means:
- two **workflow actions** after `/orchestrate`, e.g. `implement` then `review`; or
- two **orchestrator rounds**, which currently would stop after only one dispatched action.

I’d define user language as **workflow actions**, because that is what users mean by “steps”. Internally that likely means setting the effective max round to `requested_steps + 1`.

Impact on other routes should be limited if implemented this way:
- Direct `/implement`, `/review`, `/fix-pr`: no behavior change.
- Explicit `/orchestrate`: gains bounded natural-language stopping.
- Label-triggered or dispatch-triaged orchestrate: can share the same parser if `request_text` contains a limit.
- Heuristic/manual orchestrate mode: should use the parsed budget deterministically, since the planner may not run there.

Execution plan:
1. Add a small parser/helper for requested step limits from `request_text`.
2. Apply it in [`dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts) or early in [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts).
3. Clamp it against `AGENT_AUTOMATION_MAX_ROUNDS`.
4. Pass the effective limit through existing `automation_max_rounds`.
5. Update orchestrator prompt wording to explicitly respect user-requested step limits.
6. Add tests in the existing orchestrator/handoff test suites.

I’d proceed with that implementation after approval.
Closing because this agent issue has had no activity for 30 days.

title: In orchestrate, there should also be an explicit "stop" step
